flash.title: US and China readouts diverge on trade call ahead of Shenzhen APEC
flash.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent and USTR Greer held a call with Vice Premier He Lifeng on Friday. The US side pressed China on full and immediate implementation of its commitments and voiced concern about recent Chinese actions, while MOFCOM's readout described He as raising serious concerns about new US restrictive measures and called the talks frank and constructive. APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen on November 18-19, and a trilateral with Trump, Xi and Putin is reported as possible but is not confirmed.

flash.title: EU kill-switch tool: Brussels adds pressure on chemicals and machinery
flash.body: Trade Commissioner Šefčovič says the proposed kill-switch tool should be presented by the end of the year. Update since yesterday: EU leaders have asked the Commission to consider quotas and tariffs on Chinese chemicals and machinery imports, and media reports point to further import caps or tariffs as early as Q1 2027. Beijing's response, as reported, rejects politicising trade and warns of retaliation.

flash.title: Taiwan: PLA air activity rises, no named exercise announced
flash.body: Taiwan's MND counted 85 PLA aerial sorties from October 26 to November 1, up 85 percent on the prior week, per Taiwan Security Monitor. A Taiwanese defence analyst describes the recent surge as a quiet, unannounced exercise, and expects the carrier Shandong in a long-range drill around mid-November. Reports of a possible large exercise around Taiwan remain unconfirmed by any announcement.

flash.title: Affiliates Rule suspension formalised to January 10, 2027
flash.body: BIS released a final rule on November 5 formally extending the suspension of the Affiliates Rule to January 10, 2027. The rule does not otherwise modify the Affiliates Rule or act on public comments, which BIS says it will consider in future rulemakings. Practitioners warn that China's global rare-earth controls and the Affiliates Rule could both take effect in January if no permanent bilateral deal is reached.

flash.title: Beijing steps up Middle East and Mekong diplomacy
flash.body: Wang Yi met Iran's Ali Bagheri Kani on November 2, and Xi and Oman's Sultan Haitham held talks during a Gulf visit. The MFA said on November 4 that China is ready to step up communication with Saudi Arabia, Iran and other regional states as tensions escalate, and argued military means are not the answer. The 11th Lancang-Mekong Foreign Ministers' Meeting was held in Beijing on November 4.

flash.title: State Council stresses fiscal-financial coordination and capital market stability
flash.body: Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council executive meeting on November 6. The meeting called for using policy funds to leverage fiscal-financial coordination for domestic demand, defusing local government debt and small bank risks, and improving the capital market stabilisation mechanism. It also ordered study of next year's economic work plan.

flash.title: MFA asked to comment on reported block of SoftBank bid for ABB robotics
flash.body: At the November 5 MFA briefing, AFP cited a Financial Times report that China told SoftBank it will not allow its acquisition of ABB's robotics division to proceed and asked Beijing to confirm or comment. I could not retrieve the spokesperson's answer, so the status of the deal is unverified.

flash.title: Trade momentum strong; October trade data due November 10
flash.body: China's September goods trade reached a record 5.16 trillion yuan, with exports up 29.6 percent in yuan terms, and exports to the US rose sharply. Reuters-sourced reporting put September exports up 36.3 percent in dollar terms, the fastest since February. The October customs release is scheduled for November 10.

flash.title: Commercial launches continue: CERES-2 Y3 and Lijian-2 Y2
flash.body: Galactic Energy's CERES-2 Y3 launched from Jiuquan on November 7, carrying four satellites to a 535 km sun-synchronous orbit. A Lijian-2 Y2 rocket launched a new satellite group from the Dongfeng commercial space pilot zone on November 3.

flash.title: Hong Kong national security case: MFA backs prosecution
flash.body: At its November 5 briefing, the MFA said a defendant in a Hong Kong national security case pleaded guilty after facing overwhelming evidence. It said the central government firmly supports the HKSAR in punishing acts that endanger national security.

leadership.title: MFA briefings and senior diplomacy
bullets: Wang Yi met Iran's Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council on November 2, and met Thailand's foreign minister and Myanmar's planning minister on November 3.
Mao Ning's November 4 briefing said China is in communication about a possible meeting of three heads of state, without naming them.
Guo Jiakun's November 5 briefing addressed Hong Kong national security and the reported ABB robotics question.

leadership.title: State Council executive meeting, November 6
bullets: Li Qiang chaired the meeting, focusing on fiscal-financial coordination and local government debt risks.
Meeting ordered capital market stabilisation mechanism improvements and study of next year's economic work.

leadership.title: White paper: More Just and Equitable Global Governance: China's Principles, Proposals and Actions (background, published June 17, 2026)
bullets: Issued by the State Council Information Office; promotes the Global Governance Initiative.
Frames global governance as a matter of justice rather than deal-making and calls for a roadmap and timeline for joint action.

leadership.title: White paper: Hong Kong: Safeguarding China's National Security Under the Framework of One Country, Two Systems (background, published February 10, 2026)
bullets: Issued by the State Council Information Office with a preface, five parts and a conclusion.
Asserts central government jurisdiction over national security in Hong Kong and says the SAR is steady despite external challenges.

leadership.title: Policy document: Interim Measures on anthropomorphic AI interaction services (background, issued April 2026)
bullets: Issued by the CAC with four partner agencies; the CAC published the draft on April 10, 2026.
Covers AI companions and emotional-interaction services, with consumer protection, minors and elderly safeguards; listed as effective July 15, 2026 by one tracker.

leadership.title: Policy document: Implementation opinions on intelligent agents (background, May 8, 2026)
bullets: Jointly issued by the CAC, NDRC and MIIT; treats agentic AI as a separately regulated category.
Covers standardised application and innovative development of intelligent agents.
Chinese readouts of the He Lifeng call stress 'frank, in-depth and constructive' talks and objections to US restrictive measures, while US readouts stress compliance.
MFA messaging on the UK says Britain is rehashing hacking allegations as a pretext to curb China's AI development.
MFA frames Middle East diplomacy as dialogue and deescalation, rejecting military solutions.
MFA frames Hong Kong national security prosecutions as lawful and supported by the central government.
state_media.temperature: My read: the tone is confident and conciliatory toward Washington ahead of APEC, while still pushing back on EU trade defence and Western criticism of AI.

watchlist.event: Original end of the one-year Affiliates Rule suspension; BIS has extended it to January 10, 2027.
China's October trade data release (per Trading Economics calendar); CIIE in Shanghai closes.
Possible long-range PLA naval drill involving the carrier Shandong, per Taiwan analyst expectations.
APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen; possible Xi-Trump meeting, with a Putin trilateral unconfirmed.
G20 summit in Miami, where Trump has said he expects to meet Xi.
Trade truce and Affiliates Rule suspension expire unless extended.
